newsitem.title: USA: US Sen. Daschle says won't hold up nuclear bill.
newsitem.headline: US Sen. Daschle says won't hold up nuclear bill.

text.p: Senate Democrat Leader Tom Daschle said Tuesday the minority party would not hold up nuclear waste legislation after he was assured Republicans would move ahead on the chemical weapons ban treaty.
Daschle, of South Dakota, had earlier advocated holding up any non-emergency legislation until the chemical weapons ban treaty was brought to the floor for a vote.

"We are not going to do what I suggested we may be required to do this morning," Daschle said. He said he expected Democrats to join Republicans in voting late this afternoon on a motion to move ahead on the nuclear waste bill.
Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott of Mississippi said there was a chance the chemical weapons ban treaty would be brought up for a vote before April 29.
Lott also said he had made it clear that any delay on the nuclear waste bill would delay action on the chemical weapons ban treaty.
